questions.question: Which value is a hyperparameter rather than a parameter learned inside a linear model?
options: A fitted regression weight
The intercept after optimization
The learning rate chosen before training
A residual computed from a training row
questions.explanation: The learning rate controls the optimization procedure and is selected outside the fitted model parameters.

questions.question: A grid contains 3 learning rates and 2 regularization strengths. How many combinations does a full grid search evaluate?
Why can random search be more efficient than a grid when only one of many hyperparameters matters strongly?
options: Random draws explore more distinct values along the important dimension
Random search always evaluates fewer models than the requested budget
A grid cannot tune a numeric learning rate
Random search uses the test labels to select each draw
questions.explanation: A grid spends many trials repeating similar values in unimportant dimensions; random samples cover the influential dimension more broadly.

questions.question: In Bayesian optimization, what does an acquisition function choose?
options: The final test label for the current model
The next hyperparameter point by trading off predicted value and uncertainty
The number of classes from the training set
A preprocessing column without evaluating a model
questions.explanation: The surrogate predicts promising regions and uncertainty; the acquisition rule balances exploiting high predictions with exploring uncertain points.

questions.question: You tried hundreds of settings on one validation set. What protects the final estimate from tuning overfit?
options: Choose the configuration with the largest training error
Use the same validation labels as the model's training targets
Keep a test set untouched until the selected configuration is finalized
Report the best validation score as an unbiased test score
questions.explanation: Repeatedly selecting on a validation set adapts to its noise. A held-out test set or nested cross-validation gives a cleaner final estimate.

questions.question: In this lesson's search functions, what does a larger validation score mean when the objective is neg_mse?
options: The model has a larger mean squared error on the validation rows
The candidate was scored with the held-out test rows
The candidate has a smaller validation mean squared error
The search evaluated fewer configurations than its history records
questions.explanation: neg_mse returns the negative mean squared error, so values closer to zero are better and the search selects the maximum score in its history.
